audit.why: 51.48% over 1080 games — the largest sample in this slice — marked TRICKY. The chart is well shaped: Sylas takes level 1 and level 6, Camille takes 3-5 and the item stages, and the text is honest that the late game drifts back to him. Nothing to move.

The level-6 call is the standout and it is correct and unusually subtle: Hijack takes Camille's own R, and the danger is not a teamfight swing (Camille's R is a poor steal for him) but the free leap and lockdown it gives him onto her. Hijack is 80s at rank 1 falling to 30s, so baiting it in a skirmish is a real plan and the number belongs in the text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two slot errors. (a) spikes[3].text writes 'his Q/W (Petricite Burst / Kingslayer) drain' — Petricite Burst is Sylas's PASSIVE, not his Q. (b) Chain Lash is called 'drain poke' in early and whys[0] and 'Chain Lash poke and Kingslayer W heal' in wants.foe[1] — Chain Lash does damage and slows, it does not heal him. Sylas's E is never named, only called 'his E chain-dash'.
audit.why: Riot's kit is Petricite Burst (P), Chain Lash (Q), Kingslayer (W), Abscond (E), Hijack (R). All of Sylas's healing in a lane trade comes from Kingslayer — a single 12s-at-rank-1 ability falling to 6s at rank 5 — which is precisely why Grievous Wounds is decisive here and why 'force the all-in on his W heal cooldown' is the right instruction. Attributing the drain to his Q and his passive spreads the sustain across three abilities and makes anti-heal look optional when it is the answer. Abscond is 13s at rank 1 to 9s, against Hookshot's 16s.
audit.corrected: Petricite Burst corrected to the passive slot and the drain re-attributed to Kingslayer alone; Chain Lash restated as damage and slow; Abscond named with its 13s; Kingslayer's 12s given so 'on his W cooldown' is actionable.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Only commit when your E is up and his is down' and 'force the all-in on his W heal cooldown' both name cooldowns without durations.
audit.why: Abscond 13s vs Hookshot 16s means his dash is back first at rank 1 — the window is narrower than the text suggests, and it closes further as he ranks E. Kingslayer at 12s dropping to 6s means the anti-heal window shrinks fast, which is the real argument for closing the lane early.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer tldr already says 'Anti-heal his W' but the content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds at all.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags Kingslayer sustain for this matchup specifically. The two layers should agree, and the content layer is what a player reads on the loading screen.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds cue added to late and spikes[3].text.
